newsitem.title: UK: Polar to start Manchester-Korea cargo services.
newsitem.headline: Polar to start Manchester-Korea cargo services.

text.p: Polar Air Cargo said it will commence operating twice-weekly Boeing 747-200 freighter flights linking Manchester and Amsterdam with Korea and Japan from May 17.
Privately-owned Polar's UK sales director Steve Lewis told Reuters that the most important UK market that would result from the new services' launch would be Korea, both outbound and inbound.
Routeing of the first flight will be Kansai-Seoul-Anchorage, across the North Atlantic to Manchester and on to Amsterdam, returning to Kansai via Anchorage and Seoul.

The second service will be operated Kansai-Seoul-Anchorage-Manchester-Amsterdam, continuing onward to Dubai and Delhi, returning to Dubai and then flying to Amsterdam, New York-JFK, Anchorage and Seoul.
"The UK-Korea airfreight market has always been strong in both directions and I see no problem in filling the capacity that will be made available," Lewis said in a telephone interview.
"Korea will be more important than Japan as a market for us in the UK and I think the same will be the case in Continental Europe," he said.

Lewis added that Polar UK would be allocated some 30 percent of the 100 tonnes capacity available on each of the two new weekly ex-Europe flights, with the carrier's Continental stations sharing the rest of the space.
"There are difficulties in obtaining slots (at southern UK airports) but a major reason for the selection of Manchester was its ideal central location," he noted.

"There are now several Korean companies either established or opening up plants in the north-east and north-west of England and in Wales," he said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706; fax +5017
